packageRules.description: Keep required_version a compatibility floor (OpenTofu releases lag Terraform's numbering)
RKE2 versions carry a +rke2rN build suffix. Kubernetes upgrades one minor at a time, so propose each minor separately
Rancher 2.15.x requires Kubernetes < 1.37; raise this with the Rancher pin
Rancher's own charts follow its minor (110.x is Rancher 2.15); raise this with the Rancher pin

Minor and major platform updates need a human decision on compatibility and upgrade order. Patches automerge after the E2E workflow deploys them on the runner. The manual-review label (replacing the automerge one the patch/minor rules set) is what the shared preset's PR note and the PR list read

A Rancher minor is a major release of this repository (VERSIONING.md in mbologna/.github, pattern A: tags are vX.Y.Z+up<rancher>). It drops Kubernetes minors and changes the bundled Turtles and providers, so the update is committed as a breaking feat, which auto-release turns into a major.

rancher_version in ansible/group_vars/all/config.yml is the one Rancher pin. The Turtles release it bundles (its build.yaml turtlesVersion) and that release's provider catalogue (config-prime.yaml) fix Turtles, core CAPI, CAPD, CAPA and CAPRKE2: the Provider sync workflow runs fleet/scripts/sync-providers.py on a Rancher update PR and commits the fleet/platform/ pins it rewrites, and the platform check deploys and provisions with them. These never follow their own releases: a standalone bump installs providers the bundled Turtles was not tested with, and validate rejects pins that differ from its catalogue. The markers stay so the dashboard still lists the versions.

RKE2 and the kind node image patches automerge, together: the required platform check provisions the Docker RKE2 example on both through Fleet, CAPI and CAPRKE2. The AWS example's RKE2 pin moves with them; nothing exercises AWS, but a patch keeps the same classes and CCM.

AWS CCM patches automerge (minors are disabled below). Its versions come from the kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws tags (customManagers), which carry dates; registry.k8s.io has none, so under the preset's timestamp-required age gates every release stayed pending for good (2026-11). A tag can precede the image's promotion, so the required validate check fails until registry.k8s.io serves the pinned image. Nothing in CI runs the CCM on AWS: a patch of the pinned line carries fixes only. The topic keeps Renovate's commit header under commitlint's 100-column limit, which the full image name exceeds.

Patches get their own update, apart from minors. Without it Renovate offers only the highest non-major release, a minor that the rule below disables, so no patch of the pinned line was ever proposed once the next minor existed (CCM v1.36.2 behind v1.37.1, 2026-11).
A new minor needs new immutable templates and a CCM migration.
